sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MID-LVL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER THE NRN HIGH PLAINS WILL ADVANCE/AMPLIFY EWD ACROSS THE DAKOTAS FRIDAY AND INTO THE UPR MS VLY/CORN BELT BY FRIDAY NIGHT. WEAK CYCLOGENESIS WILL OCCUR ALONG THE SD/ND BORDER AND MIGRATE ALONG A WARM FRONT INTO ERN MN/WRN WI BY 12Z SATURDAY. IN WAKE OF THE MID-LVL IMPULSE...A COLD FRONT WILL SWEEP SEWD...REACHING AN ERN MN...CNTRL KS AND TX PNHDL LINE BY EARLY SATURDAY MORNING. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...A MYRIAD OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES WILL EXIST FROM NRN MO NWWD INTO SRN NEB WITH AN MCV TRAVELING EWD FROM IA TOWARD IL BY FRIDAY EVENING. BOTH THE SYNOPTIC COLD FRONT AND OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL BE INSTIGATORS OF PSBL SVR TSTMS FRI AND FRI NIGHT.

sections.title: UPR MS VLY SWWD INTO THE SRN PLAINS/OZARKS
sections.text: SVRL AREAS OF SVR WEATHER WILL BE PSBL THROUGH THE DAY 1 PD IN A COMPLEX SFC PATTERN. HIGHEST SVR POTENTIAL WILL LIKELY EVOLVE ACROSS PORTIONS OF CNTRL/ERN KS INTO THE OZARKS/NERN OK DURING THE AFTN. ALTHOUGH WEAKENING EARLY FRI MORNING...BACKBUILDING PORTION OF AN MCS OVER THE MID-MO VLY WILL LIKELY INTENSIFY DURING THE AFTN AS SRN PORTION OF THE MID-LVL WAVE OVER THE NRN PLAINS GRAZES THE REGION. AIR MASS ALONG/SW OF THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY WILL BECOME VERY UNSTABLE AS MID-UPR 60S SFC DEW POINTS ARE MAINTAINED/COUPLED WITH STRONG HEATING. INCREASING WNW FLOW IN THE MID/UPR LVLS /AOA 40 KTS/ WILL ENCOURAGE STORMS TO FORWARD PROPAGATE ALONG THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT WITH PREFERENTIAL DEVELOPMENT INTO THE HOT BOUNDARY LAYER ACROSS CNTRL-ERN KS /PSBL SUPERCELLS WITH VERY LARGE HAIL/. ACTIVITY WILL LIKELY REACH THE OZARKS AND PORTIONS OF CNTRL/ERN OK LATE FRI EVE OR EARLY SATURDAY WITH SVR WINDS/HAIL. MEANWHILE...A SEPARATE AREA OF SVR POTENTIAL MAY EVOLVE ACROSS THE ERN DAKOTAS EWD INTO PORTIONS OF THE UPR MS VLY ASSOCIATED WITH THE PRIMARY UPR TROUGH. THERE WILL LIKELY BE CONSIDERABLE CLOUD DEBRIS/ONGOING WARM ADVECTION-DERIVED TSTM CLUSTERS OVER THE REGION DURING THE DAY. SOME OF THESE

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: MODERATE WNW FLOW WILL PREVAIL FROM THE NRN/CNTRL PLNS TO THE E CST THIS PERIOD...ALONG NERN FRINGE OF ELONGATED ANTICYCLONE CENTERED OVER THE FOUR CORNERS REGION. WITHIN THIS FLOW...A SHORTWAVE TROUGH NOW ALONG THE MT/ND BORDER WILL AMPLIFY SEWD...REACHING SE ND THIS EVE AND SW MN EARLY SAT. S OF THE TROUGH...A SERIES OF WEAKER DISTURBANCES WILL TRACK FROM THE CNTRL HI PLNS TO THE MID MS VLY. FEATURES WILL REMAIN WEAK AT LWR LVLS...AND SOMEWHAT OBSCURED BY CONVECTIVE OUTFLOW. A WEAK CYCLONE LOOSELY ASSOCIATED WITH THE MT/ND IMPULSE WILL MOVE FROM ERN SD THIS MORNING TO SE MN/WRN WI BY 12Z SAT. IN THE WAKE OF THE IMPULSE...A COLD FRONT WILL EVOLVE OVER THE DAKOTAS LATER TODAY. THE BOUNDARY SHOULD ACCELERATE SEWD TONIGHT/EARLY SATURDAY...AND EXTEND FROM ERN MN THROUGH CNTRL KS TO THE TX PNHDL LINE BY 12Z SATURDAY. AHEAD OF THE FRONT...THE WARM SECTOR WILL BE COMPLICATED BY SEVERAL OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES FROM SRN/ERN SD SWD INTO AND NRN MO. THESE BOUNDARIES...AND THE COLD FRONT...WILL FOCUS STRONG TO SVR STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE PERIOD.

sections.title: CNTRL/SRN PLNS AND OZARKS INTO THE UPR MS VLY TODAY/TNGT
sections.text: SEVERAL AREAS OF SVR STORMS MAY EVOLVE THROUGH EARLY SAT ALONG AND AHEAD OF THE AFOREMENTIONED SFC BOUNDARIES. THE GREATEST SVR POTENTIAL SHOULD EVOLVE THIS AFTN OVER CNTRL/ERN KS S/SE INTO THE OZARKS/NE OK AS SFC HEATING DESTABILIZES FAIRLY MOIST WARM SECTOR BENEATH BROAD EML PLUME ON S SIDE OF AMPLIFYING UPR IMPULSE. THE STORMS LIKELY WILL ARISE AS REINTENSIFICATION OF AND/OR WWD REDEVELOPMENT OF LINGERING OVERNIGHT CONVECTION. COMBINATION OF STRONG INSTABILITY /SBCAPE 3000-4000 J PER KG/ WITH INCREASING /30 TO 40 KT/ WNW FLOW ON SRN FRINGE OF UPR IMPULSE SHOULD FOSTER STORM ORGANIZATION/SUSTENANCE. IN ADDITION TO A FEW SUPERCELLS CAPABLE OF VERY LARGE HAIL AND POSSIBLY A SHORT LIVED TORNADO OR TWO...THE ACTIVITY SHOULD ORGANIZE INTO FORWARD PROPAGATING CLUSTERS AND BANDS...ESPECIALLY ALONG THE INSTABILITY GRADIENT IN KS. THE STORMS SHOULD REACH THE OZARKS AND PARTS OF CNTRL/ERN OK LATE THIS EVE OR EARLY SAT WITH SVR WIND AND HAIL. PARTS OF THIS REGION MAY REQUIRE UPGRADE TO MODERATE RISK WHEN/IF IT BECOMES MORE APPARENT EXACTLY WHERE THE MOST STRONGEST FORWARD-PROPAGATING LINE SEGMENTS MAY DEVELOP. A SEPARATE SVR STORM AREA MAY EVOLVE OVER THE ERN DAKOTAS EWD INTO THE UPR MS VLY

sections.title: KS/MO/OK/AR
sections.text: WEAKLY ORGANIZED MCS AND ASSOCIATED STRONG OUTFLOW HAVE SPREAD ACROSS MUCH OF NERN KS AND NWRN MO THIS MORNING AND RESULTED IN CONSIDERABLE STABILIZATION OF THE BOUNDARY LAYER OVER NEB AND IA. ANOTHER CLUSTER OF ELEVATED CONVECTION HAS DEVELOPED GENERALLY EAST ALONG THE KS/OK BORDER ASSOCIATED WITH WEAK WARM ADVECTION AND MASS TRANSPORT ON THE NOSE OF 20-25 KT LLJ WHERE CAPPING IS SOMEWHAT WEAKER. THERE ARE AT LEAST TWO AREAS OF CONCERN FOR SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT THROUGH THE LATE AFTERNOON. THE FIRST WILL BE ACROSS PORTIONS OF MO AHEAD OF THE PERSISTING AND WEAKLY ORGANIZED MCS OUTFLOW DEVELOPING SEWD FROM ERN KS AND NWRN MO. VISIBLE SATL IMAGERY AND OBS INDICATE STRONG SURFACE HEATING IS UNDERWAY ACROSS MUCH OF CNTRL/SRN MO AHEAD OF THE OUTFLOW/DECAYING MCS. BASED ON SGF MORNING SOUNDING...MLCAPE WILL CONTINUE TO RISE ABOVE 1000 J/KG AS TEMPERATURES CLIMB THROUGH THE 80S. GENERALLY WEAKER CAPPING ACROSS MO SHOULD BE OVERCOME THROUGH A COMBINATION OF HEATING...INCREASINGLY SUPPORTIVE LARGE SCALE ASCENT/WEAK HEIGHT FALLS...AND LIFT ALONG OUTFLOW SURGE AND DIFFERENTIAL HEATING BOUNDARIES. ONCE SURFACE-BASED STORM DEVELOPMENT OCCURS...EFFECTIVE SHEAR ACROSS THE REGION IS FORECAST TO

sections.title: DAKOTAS/MN
sections.text: WELL-DEFINED SHORT WAVE TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED SURFACE LOW AND FRONT WILL DEVELOP EAST INTO A GRADUALLY DESTABILIZING AIRMASS FROM THE ERN DAKOTAS INTO MN LATER TODAY. AT PRESENT...GREATER INSTABILITY DEVELOPING BENEATH THE MID/UPPER LOW IN ND IS SOMEWHAT REMOVED FROM STRONGER SHEAR ASSOCIATED WITH THE 40-5OKT MID LEVEL SPEED MAX ACROSS SD. HOWEVER...WITH TIME...EXPECT THAT LARGE SCALE ASCENT AND LIFT NEAR THE LOW AND ADVANCING FRONT ACROSS THE REGION WILL LEAD TO MORE CONVECTION IN THE FORM OF MULTICELL...AND PERHAPS A COUPLE OF SUPERCELL...STORMS. MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL IS LIKELY TO BE THE PRIMARY THREAT BUT A FEW WIND EVENTS ALSO APPEAR POSSIBLE AT THE HEIGHT OF STORM DEVELOPMENT/INTENSITY LATER TODAY.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST
sections.text: VERY WEAK RESIDUAL FRONTAL ZONE WAS SITUATED FROM SERN NC WWD ACROSS THE DEEP SOUTH AND LIES WITHIN A VERY MOIST AND INCREASINGLY UNSTABLE AIRMASS. POST-FRONTAL ELY FLOW ACROSS ERN NC WAS TOPPED BY 15-20KT WLY MID LEVEL FLOW RESULTING IN SUFFICIENT EFFECTIVE SHEAR IN THIS AREA FOR A FEW MORE PERSISTENT UPDRAFTS CAPABLE OF PRODUCING HAIL. STORM COVERAGE WILL INCREASE ACROSS MUCH OF THE SOUTH AND SOUTHEAST AS WEAK INHIBITION IS OVERCOME BY DIURNAL HEATING. GENERALLY LIMITED FLOW/SHEAR SHOULD PRECLUDE A MORE WIDESPREAD SEVERE WEATHER DAY BUT A NUMBER OF STORMS COULD GENERATE LOCALIZED DAMAGING DOWNBURSTS ALONG WITH MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL AROUND AN INCH IN DIAMETER. ..CARBIN.. 08/12/2011

sections.title: KS/MO/OK/AR/WRN TN
sections.text: AT 19Z...OUTFLOW BOUNDARY FROM MORNING/ONGOING CONVECTION STRETCHED FROM CENTRAL MO SWWD TO JUST NORTH OF THE OK/KS BORDER...AND THEN NWWD TO A WEAK SURFACE LOW NEAR DDC. SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN KEPT FOR PORTIONS OF THE AREA NORTH OF THE BOUNDARY AS WARM ADVECTION ABOVE COOLER BOUNDARY LAYER MAY GENERATE ELEVATED STORMS WITH SEVERE HAIL THIS AFTERNOON/EVENING. THE MOST INTENSE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP NEAR THE OUTFLOW BOUNDARY/SURFACE LOW SHORTLY...AND THEN SPREAD ESEWD/SEWD WITHIN WNWLY FLOW ALOFT AND STRONGER INSTABILITY. HAIL AND EVENTUAL EVOLUTION TO LINEAR COMPLEX/BOW ECHO IS EXPECTED BY LATE TODAY...REFERENCE MD 1957 AND WW 772. STORMS FROM CENTRAL MO SEWD INTO SERN KS MAY ALSO EVOLVE INTO A COMPLEX LATER THIS EVENING AS WINDS ALOFT INCREASE AND AIR MASS CONTINUES TO DESTABILIZE ACROSS FAR SRN MO/NRN AR. THE SLIGHT RISK HAS BEEN EXTENDED SLIGHTLY FURTHER SEWD INTO THE WRN TN VALLEY FOR POTENTIAL COMPLEX TO DEVELOP AND REACH THE WRN TN VALLEY LATE TONIGHT...AS DEPICTED BY SOME STORM SCALE MODELS.

sections.title: DAKOTAS/UPPER MS VALLEY
sections.text: STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS WERE OCCURRING IN ERN ND IN ASSOCIATION WITH UPPER CIRCULATION. THESE STORMS ARE EXPECTED TO EXPAND SEWD INTO MN...BEFORE GRADUALLY WEAKENING THIS EVENING WITH LOSS OF HEATING/INSTABILITY. ALTHOUGH WARM ADVECTION WILL ALSO GENERATE STORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF SERN MN/SRN WI...SEVERE WEATHER PROBABILITIES WERE LOWERED IN THIS AREA DUE TO VERY MARGINAL INSTABILITY. ..IMY.. 08/12/2011 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1138 AM CDT FRI AUG 12 2011/ CORRECTED GENERAL THUNDERSTORM GRAPHIC

sections.title: SCNTRL KS INTO OK
sections.text: COMPLEX ARRAY OF OUTFLOW BOUNDARIES EXIST ACROSS SCNTRL KS/OK THIS EVE. PRIMARY OUTFLOW BOUNDARY...EMANATING FROM DECAYING ECNTRL OK MCS...ARCS FROM SERN OK NWWD TO TSTM CLUSTERS OVER NWRN OK. OTHER OUTFLOW HAS SURGED NWD FROM LATE AFTN STORMS OVER CNTRL OK. OBJECTIVE/ MESOANALYSIS/00Z OUN SOUNDING SUGGEST THAT MORE PRISTINE AIR MASS...CHARACTERIZED BY MLCAPE TO 2500 J/KG...IS PLACED OVER NWRN/NCNTRL/WCNTRL OK...WITH MORE STABLE ENVIRONMENT FARTHER EAST. EXPECT TSTM CLUSTERS OVER SCNTRL KS/NWRN OK WILL PROPAGATE INTO THE AFOREMENTIONED INSTABILITY RESERVOIR. WNW FLOW ALOFT IN COMBINATION WITH VERY UNSTABLE AIR MASS WILL RESULT IN BOWS WITH POSSIBLE CORRIDORS OF VERY HIGH WINDS IN NWRN-NCNTRL OK ALONG/S OF THE PRIMARY OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. THIS ACTIVITY...AND ADDITIONAL WARM ADVECTION-DERIVED STORMS...WILL CONTINUE ESE ACROSS CNTRL/SCNTRL/SERN OK OVERNIGHT. WHILE HIGHER SVR/HAIL WIND PROBABILITIES SHOULD BE CONFINED TO NEAR-TERM ACTIVITY IN NWRN/NCNTRL OK...THOSE SVR THREATS WILL PROBABLY BE CARRIED SEWD TOWARD THE RED RVR OVERNIGHT.

sections.title: MID-SOUTH
sections.text: MCV WAS MOVING ESE NEAR THE OH/MS RVR CONFLUENCE EARLY THIS EVE WITH A TRAILING BAND OF TSTMS INTO NRN AR. 00Z LZK SOUNDING EXHIBITS MLCAPE OF 4230 J/KG WITH DCAPE IN EXCESS OF 1200 J/KG...SUPPORTIVE OF CONTINUED STORM MAINTENANCE THROUGH THE EVENING. WHILE NERN EXTENT OF LINE SEGMENT SHOULD WEAKEN OVER FAR W KY/NWRN TN...STORMS WILL LIKELY CONTINUE ESE ACROSS CNTRL/ERN AR...WRN TN AND PERHAPS NWRN MS OVERNIGHT. FAVORED WNWLY FLOW...ALBEIT WEAK...COMBINED WITH THERMODYNAMICS AT HAND WILL YIELD OCNL BOWING STRUCTURES WITH DMGG WIND GUSTS/MRGLLY SVR HAIL.

sections.title: WRN/SRN MN
sections.text: BAND OF TSTMS CONTINUES TO PROGRESS EWD INTO WRN MN THIS EVE...ALONG A COLD FRONT. STRONGER STORMS WILL PREFER SRN END OF THE LINE ACROSS WRN/SRN MN THROUGH LATE EVENING WHERE AIR MASS WAS COMPARATIVELY WARMER TODAY. RELATIVELY COLD MID-LVL TEMPERATURES /AROUND MINUS 15 DEG C/ AND RESIDUAL LWR 60S DEW POINTS WILL CONTRIBUTE TO BRIEF PULSE-TYPE SVR STORMS WITH MRGLLY SVR HAIL AND GUSTY WINDS. ..RACY.. 08/13/2011
